ops.title: DESIGN invariant I14 is false in the tree: no inbound drain-preamble path exists
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 by the P4.3b lane-D refuter, verified exhaustively from source.

docs/DESIGN.md specifies an INBOUND drain preamble in three places:
- :487 (invariant I14, "The repair channel has no compatibility axis") — "The wire Drain verb is the
  fast path, admitted on a frozen two-byte preamble below the protocol gate and above the trust
  gate: protocol-blind, still authorized by Trust.Control (K48 intact)."
- :82-84 (Device 4) — "so a new-era successor reaches an old-era incumbent… The 18,999-handshake
  wedge has no site to occur at, twice over."
- :557 (serve ladder step 7) — "the frozen Drain preamble dispatches to the trust-gated drain path".

That path does not exist:
- `drainPreamble` is only ever WRITTEN, at internal/wire/server.go:224 and :256, both on the draining
  server's outbound path.
- `Codec.PeekPreamble` (internal/wire/codec.go:61) has exactly one non-test caller —
  `clientHandshake` at internal/wire/hello.go:137, client side.
- `readClientHello` applies the protocol gate at internal/wire/hello.go:111 BEFORE the lane switch,
  so the control lane is protocol-gated like every other lane. A protocol-1 client cannot attach a
  protocol-2 daemon's control lane at all.
- The Swift half agrees: Sources/DaemonKit/SessionTransport.swift:379 calls the two bytes what a
  draining server "emits instead of an ack".

So I14's second sentence is false: the wire Drain verb DOES have a compatibility axis. Only SIGTERM
is protocol-blind, and Device 4's "twice over" is once.

What it costs: across a protocol bump, a new-era successor cannot gracefully drain an old-era
incumbent — it falls back to SIGTERM via launchd bootout. That is precisely the capability the
18,999-handshake wedge device was designed to preserve, and deploy.Supersede drains through exactly
that window.

ROUTING: implement in the phase-4 wire-hardening lane (Lane B, fable — it already touches the
hello/handshake path for ClientConfig.Authorize, the Tenant reserved-field change, and chunk-frame
refusal). Peek before readClientHello and dispatch to the trust-gated drain path. If it is NOT
implemented, DESIGN must be corrected instead — the two must not disagree.

The mixed-era gate had been telling the truth about this (declared ABSENT since phase 2, which made
GITHUB_REF_TYPE=tag refuse); a lane briefly made it green by repointing the mechanism name at the
outbound proposition. A corrective pass restores the honest declaration and adds a structural guard
freezing each mechanism's proposition beside its name.

ops.text: Either internal/wire drains on an inbound preamble below the protocol gate and above the trust gate, or DESIGN I14 / Device 4 / the serve ladder are corrected to say the repair channel is SIGTERM plus the trust-gated control lane
ci/mixedera's drain-preamble mechanism is PROVEN for the inbound proposition, or declared unredeemed with the reason
